title: Weak point Wednesday: Rear delts
summary: He argues rear delts can be built naturally with specific strategies: a heavy compound modified to load them (snatch grip pulls) plus light, high-rep, high-frequency isolation such as face pulls and Arnold raises. Work capacity should build up over time.
claims: Rear delts, upper chest and traps can be built naturally with the right strategies; PED users grow them easily because of their many androgen receptors
You cannot rely on compound movements for rear delts; find movements that really fire them, and a weighted stretch helps
Snatch grip lifts put the rear delts under a loaded stretch
For heavy rear delt work choose a compound that involves them and modify it to accentuate them, such as snatch grip pulls from the floor or blocks, rather than heavy face pulls
Perfect isolation is not required; other muscles helping is more bang for your buck
Do face pulls with a rope or bands, playing with hand placement and external rotation; high-volume, low-intensity, high-frequency rear delt work is good for shoulder health and size
Arnold raises, from his Road to Bigger Shoulders series, stretch the rear delt at the bottom and fully contract it at the top; no lift beats them for mind-muscle connection
Needle raises target side delts more but still build the rear delts
One heavy compound plus one or two light high-rep isolation movements is all a small muscle like the rear delt needs
Rear delts start with almost no work capacity, so three isolation sets may leave them sore for three days; over time you can train them every two days or daily
Do not stay stuck isolating a small body part once every seven days; increase as it evolves
The rear delt is key for 3D shoulders, and this strategy greatly improved the look of his own
